item.title: Local editors warn government over online news plans
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Local editors warn government over online news plans
Editors from across the UK, including the editor of the Fenland Citizen, have written to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy to express concerns over proposed government plans for online news. The group argues that the suggested prominence regime is unworkable and could threaten the future of local journalism by distorting the news marketplace.
The letter highlights fears that the policy could lead to fewer local news sources for communities. Instead, the editors are calling for alternative support, such as ensuring fair payment from digital platforms and increasing government advertising spend in local titles. The signatories believe these changes are necessary to protect the sustainability of the local news ecosystem.

item.title: Teenager sentenced following high-speed police pursuit on A47
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Teenager sentenced following high-speed police pursuit on A47
An 18-year-old man has been handed a suspended prison sentence after a dangerous police pursuit across Norfolk. Ellis Rabey-Prosser, of Mildenhall, reached speeds of 100mph and drove the wrong way around a roundabout in Swaffham during the incident on October 6. The pursuit concluded when he crashed into a lamppost at the Hardwick roundabout in King’s Lynn.
Rabey-Prosser pleaded guilty to multiple charges, including dangerous driving and driving while disqualified. At Norwich Magistrates’ Court, he received a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for two years. He has also been disqualified from driving for a further two years and must pay £227 in costs. Police confirmed the driver had altered his vehicle's number plate before the pursuit began.

West Norfolk Council and King’s Lynn Town FC join forces for White Ribbon Day
West Norfolk Council and King’s Lynn Town Football Club have launched a joint campaign to tackle male violence, harassment, and abuse against women and girls. Marking White Ribbon Day, the partnership has released a video featuring players and staff encouraging the community to challenge sexist behaviour and inappropriate comments.
The initiative is part of a three-year action plan to promote a culture of respect. Officials are urging the public to speak up against abuse and are highlighting support services for victims of domestic violence. Murder investigation underway in Wisbech
Police have launched a murder investigation following the death of a 61-year-old woman in Wisbech. Officers were called to a property on Alexandra Road at 9:50pm on Saturday. A 62-year-old man, who was arrested at the scene on suspicion of murder, is currently in hospital. He is expected to remain there for a few days before being returned to police custody.
Detectives say they are not looking for anyone else in connection with the incident, which they believe to be isolated. A post-mortem examination is scheduled for Thursday. Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101, quoting Operation Emeth.

item.title: National operator First Bus acquires King’s Lynn company Lynx
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
National operator First Bus acquires King’s Lynn company Lynx
The King’s Lynn-based bus operator Lynx has been acquired by the national firm First Bus. The move aims to expand the company's network across North and West Norfolk. Lynx, which was founded in 2014, currently manages 25 routes with a fleet of 38 vehicles and 80 staff members.
The existing management team will remain in place, and Lynx will continue to operate as a separate unit within the First Bus portfolio. Founders Julian Patterson, Andy Warnes, and Steve Challis stated that the partnership will help protect the business while providing access to national investment and expertise. First Bus says it intends to build on the existing reputation of the service to encourage further bus travel in the region.

Busy month of community projects for Priory Rotary Club
The Priory Rotary Club has completed a series of community projects across the King’s Lynn area. Volunteers recently planted a new oak tree and created a wildflower bed at Wootton Park. The club also hosted its annual technology tournament for students from five local schools, and served a harvest lunch to 80 elderly residents in Dersingham.
Financial support has also been provided to several charities, including the Tapping House hospice and the Fairstead Community Shop. Looking ahead, the club is preparing for its annual Swimarathon, scheduled for February 6 at St James Pool in King’s Lynn. Those interested in joining the club or learning more about their upcoming events can visit the Priory Rotary website.

item.title: Queen Elizabeth Hospital specialist wins national mentoring award
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Queen Elizabeth Hospital specialist wins national mentoring award
A health play specialist at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been honoured with a national award. Nicola Wright received the Starlight Mentor of the Year Award 2026 at a ceremony in London on November 10. The accolade recognises her work in training the next generation of specialists who use therapeutic play to support children through medical treatment.
Ms Wright was nominated by her apprentice, Claire Burrell, who credited her mentor with building the confidence needed to succeed in the role. The hospital’s play team works across the Rudham ward, helping young patients manage fears surrounding procedures and long-term hospital stays. Chief nurse Dawn Collins praised Ms Wright for her dedication to both patient care and staff development.
